claim: A forensic audit commissioned in Purdue Pharma's bankruptcy found the Sackler family withdrew about $10.4 billion from Purdue and affiliated entities from 2008 onward, as sales of the opioid painkiller OxyContin and the overdose crisis grew. A roughly $6 billion Sackler settlement approved in 2022 was struck down by the U.S. Supreme Court in June 2024 in Harrington v. Purdue Pharma, which held the bankruptcy code did not authorize releasing the Sacklers from liability without claimants' consent. A new settlement of about $7.4 billion was reached in principle in January 2025.

notes: Corrections to the reel's figures: the withdrawal is ~$10.4 billion (AlixPartners audit, 2008 onward), not the reel's '$13 billion.' The '$6 billion they lost from getting sued' matches the 2022 revised bankruptcy-plan Sackler contribution — but the Supreme Court struck that deal (5-4, Gorsuch) on June 27, 2024, holding non-consensual third-party releases unauthorized; the operative deal since January 2025 is ~$7.4 billion. Purdue itself pleaded guilty to federal criminal charges in 2007 and again in 2020. OxyContin = Purdue's extended-release oxycodone, marketed from 1996.
